title: Hearsay or Fact? How Framing and Elicitation Shape LLM Probability Updates
title_zh: 传闻还是事实？框架与提问方式如何塑造大模型的概率更新

paragraphs.en: 总结：研究测试七种配置发现，传闻式表述会削弱大模型概率更新的方向敏感性，且降低极端值的引导方式可能同时削弱其对证据的敏感度。 Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judgment assistants and as stand-in participants in psychology experiments, yet little is known about how much their probability estimates move in response to a single new piece of information. We pair premise-hypothesis items from $δ$-SNLI with one strengthener and one weakener each, elicit the prior and the posteriors in separate calls, and measure the directional movement s: the mean posterior change signed by the annotated direction, so that the prior cancels out. We vary whether the update is stated ("Here is something else you learned") or reported ("Someone said that"), and whether the model gives one probability or five weighted estimates. We test seven configurations: two local models (Qwen3-8B, OLMo-2-7B; 240 pairs) and five configurations run through agent command-line harnesses (120 pairs), with hypotheses and analysis rules fixed before the formal runs (not publicly registered). Under stated, direct elicitation all seven move in the annotated direction (s = 18-28 percentage points). Reporting lowers s in all seven point estimates (significantly in six, by 2-5 points) and raises the share of reverse movements in all seven: the effect is consistent but small. Five weighted estimates lower the share of responses at $\leq$5% or $\geq$95% in all seven, but in the two local models they also reduce s by 43% and 68%, whereas in the harnessed configurations the point estimates of the change lie between -3.7 and +0.5 points. An elicitation format that reduces extreme values thus need not preserve sensitivity to evidence; the two should be tested separately. Because $δ$-NLI annotates only direction, we make no claim about how large an update should be. Code, data and the frozen plan: https://github.com/asj252/llm-judgment-studies
paragraphs.zh: 总结：研究测试七种配置发现，传闻式表述会削弱大模型概率更新的方向敏感性，且降低极端值的引导方式可能同时削弱其对证据的敏感度。大语言模型越来越多地被用作判断助手以及心理学实验中的替代被试，但人们对它们的概率估计在接收到一条新信息后会移动多少却知之甚少。 我们将 $δ$-SNLI 中的前提—假设条目各配以一个增强项和一个削弱项，在单独的调用中引导出先验和后验，并测量方向性移动 s：即由标注方向赋号的后验变化均值，从而使先验相互抵消。 我们变化更新是以陈述方式给出（「这是你还了解到的一件事」）还是以转述方式给出（「有人说」），以及模型给出的是一个概率还是五个加权估计。 我们测试七种配置：两个本地模型（Qwen3-8B、OLMo-2-7B；240 对）和五个通过智能体命令行框架运行的配置（120 对），假设与分析规则在正式运行前已固定（未公开预注册）。 在陈述式、直接引导下，全部七个配置都朝标注方向移动（s = 18–28 个百分点）。 转述在全部七个配置中都降低 s 的点估计（其中六个显著，降幅 2–5 个百分点），并在全部七个配置中提高反向移动的占比：该效应一致但较小。 五个加权估计在全部七个配置中都降低 $\leq$5% 或 $\geq$95% 的响应占比，但在两个本地模型中它们也使 s 分别降低 43% 和 68%，而在框架化配置中该变化的点估计介于 -3.7 到 +0.5 个百分点之间。 因此，降低极端值的引导格式未必能保持对证据的敏感度；这两者应分别检验。 由于 $δ$-NLI 仅标注方向，我们对更新应当有多大不作任何断言。 代码、数据与冻结计划：https://github.com/asj252/llm-judgment-studies
